items.summary: An open-source (MIT) memory layer for AI coding agents: it captures sessions from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode and 20+ other harnesses, normalizes them into one event model, and turns useful discoveries into reusable knowledge and skills the next session can retrieve over MCP. Local-first with a free cloud tier; it hit #1 Product of the Day on its November 2 launch and has passed 3,200 GitHub stars.
items.title: beacon.sh: Open-source memory layer for coding agents, turning sessions across 20+ harnesses into shared knowledge (#1 on Product Hunt, Nov 2)

items.summary: A proactive agent for business work that runs on your own machine, powered by the AI subscriptions you already pay for — Claude Code, Codex and more, or hosted models. It carries long-running workflows forward in the background, surfaces only the decisions that need you, gates sensitive actions behind signoffs, and connects over MCP, WhatsApp, Gmail, Outlook and phone; available for Mac (Apple Silicon), Windows and Linux, with the core under BSL 1.1.
items.title: qorqbot: A proactive agent that runs on your own machine, carrying long tasks forward on subscriptions you already pay for (public Nov 2, early preview)

items.summary: Coding agents can write an iPhone app but can't build one without a Mac: NoMac lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP client rent an Apple Silicon cloud Mac (ready in about 30 seconds) with one line, then build, run the iOS Simulator, read its screen, sign and submit to TestFlight and the App Store. It costs $0.90 an hour, billed by the minute with no subscription; the maker's demo build cost 3 cents.
items.title: NoMac: Rent an AI agent its own cloud Mac with Xcode and an iOS Simulator, billed by the minute (Product Hunt, Nov 8)
